finding: Of 39,158 paid invoices, 16,418 (41.9%) were late; 8,271 were on time and 14,469 were early. Median delay was 0 days.
business_interpretation: A material share of settlements arrive after due date, even though the median of all paid invoices is on time (zero days). Separate early, on-time and late behaviour rather than relying on the average alone.
ml_hypothesis: A binary late-payment classifier using only information available by invoice/due date can identify elevated late-payment risk.

finding: Among terms with at least 100 paid invoices, NAX2 had the highest late rate (99.8%, n=540).
business_interpretation: Observed repayment behaviour differs strongly by the coded payment-term category. The code labels are not decoded in the source, so their business meanings need mentor confirmation.
ml_hypothesis: Payment-term code is a useful categorical predictor; compare it with a baseline model and use frequency-aware validation.

finding: Paid invoices due on Sunday and Saturday had late rates of 59.7% and 58.0%, versus 32.6% for Wednesday.
business_interpretation: Calendar-day delay may be elevated when contractual due dates fall on weekends; this may reflect settlement calendars rather than purely customer intent.
ml_hypothesis: Due weekday and weekend/holiday indicators may improve prediction; test a business-day-adjusted lateness target as a sensitivity analysis.

finding: There were 9,681 open invoices (19.8% of records); 9,181 were overdue at the analytical cut-off 2020-05-22. Open amount by currency: CAD 42,218,190.72; USD 280,875,125.47.
business_interpretation: Unpaid exposure is material. Currency totals must remain separate until a valid FX rate and conversion date are supplied.
ml_hypothesis: A cash-collection prioritization model can rank open invoices by predicted settlement risk and amount, while preserving currency-specific reporting.

finding: The 31-60 days overdue bucket contained 4,427 open invoices, the largest overdue aging group.
business_interpretation: Collections operations should focus on invoices that have moved beyond 30 days overdue, with prioritization by amount and customer-level risk.
ml_hypothesis: A multi-class aging-risk model or time-to-payment model may help forecast migration into 31-60, 61-90 and 90+ day buckets.

finding: Among customer IDs with at least 20 paid invoices, the highest late-rate customer in this extract was CCU013 (100.0%; n=534). 219 customer IDs met the 20-invoice threshold.
business_interpretation: Historical payment behaviour varies by customer. Group by customer ID rather than customer name because names are not consistent within IDs in this dataset.
ml_hypothesis: Use leakage-safe historical customer aggregates (prior late rate, prior average delay, prior invoice count), computed only from earlier invoices.

finding: Spearman correlation between amount and delay was 0.078 for USD and -0.085 for CAD paid invoices.
business_interpretation: Invoice size alone has a weak monotonic relationship with payment delay in both currencies; other behavioural and contractual factors likely matter more.
ml_hypothesis: Amount may need nonlinear transforms and interactions; combine with payment terms, customer history, and calendar features rather than using it alone.

finding: Invoice volume peaked in 2020-03 (4,674 invoices), but the later months are dominated by open records; only months with at least 100 paid invoices are used for the paid-delay trend (through 2020-02).
business_interpretation: Recent invoices have not all settled, so completed-payment delay trends are right-censored and should not be interpreted as a true improvement or deterioration.
ml_hypothesis: Use a time-based split and consider survival/time-to-event methods or censoring-aware evaluation for open invoices.

finding: Invoices created in the last 3 days of a month had a 43.1% late rate vs 41.8% otherwise; last-5-day quarter-end invoices had 43.1% vs 41.9% otherwise.
business_interpretation: The differences are modest in this sample. Calendar-end effects may be worth testing, but current evidence does not establish a large operational effect.
ml_hypothesis: Add month-end and quarter-end flags as candidate features and retain them only if they improve time-split validation.

finding: Invoice amount is strongly right-skewed; 2,460 rows were flagged by the Week 1 IQR outlier rule and retained.
business_interpretation: A small number of large invoices can materially affect averages and receivable exposure. Outlier flags should support review, not automatic deletion.
ml_hypothesis: Compare log1p(amount), robust scaling and tree-based models; evaluate error separately across amount bands.
